points.text: States the verdict: do not reject the null hypothesis
Gives the reason: the p-value 0.31 is greater than alpha = 0.05, so the data is not surprising enough under the null to reject it

items.prompt: A hypothesis test at the 5% significance level returns a p-value of 0.31. State the test verdict and give the reason.

points.text: Describes a Type I error: rejecting a true null - declaring the machine miscalibrated when it is actually fine
Describes a Type II error: accepting a false null - passing the machine when it is actually miscalibrated - and states alpha caps the probability of a Type I error

items.prompt: In a quality test, the null hypothesis says a machine is calibrated. Describe a Type I error and a Type II error in this context, and state which error's probability is capped by the significance level alpha.

points.text: Sets dy/dx = 0 and solves to x = 1 and x = 3

items.prompt: A curve has equation y = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x. Find dy/dx and the x-coordinates of its stationary points.

points.text: Writes A = pi r^2 and applies the chain rule dA/dt = 2 pi r dr/dt
Substitutes r = 4 and dr/dt = 0.5 to give 4 pi cm^2/s

items.prompt: The radius of a circle increases at 0.5 cm/s. Find the rate at which its area increases when the radius is 4 cm.

levels.descriptor: Methods are chosen and applied exactly, p-values are compared with alpha explicitly, and conclusions are justified without assigning a probability to the null.
levels.label: Secure

levels.descriptor: Method is correct in outline but a comparison, error-type definition or substitution step is skipped.
levels.label: Developing

levels.descriptor: Methods are misapplied - for example reading a p-value of 0.03 as a 3% chance the null is true - and the working does not support the answer.
levels.label: Beginning
